newsitem.title: GERMANY: WCM not interested in Karstadt stake-paper.
newsitem.headline: WCM not interested in Karstadt stake-paper.

text.p: Germany's WCM Beteiligungs und Grundbesitz-AG on Wednesday was reported as saying it was no longer interested in buying a one-quarter stake in department store group Karstadt AG.
"We have put acquiring a stake in Karstadt behind us," WCM majority shareholder Karl Ehlerding told the Handelsblatt business daily, in a report to be published on Thursday.
WCM had expressed an interest in buying stakes of 10 percent each in Karstadt held by Deutsche Bank AG and Commerzbank AG, but pulled out after finding the banks' asking price too high.
Efforts to buy a further five percent via the German stock market also failed because of a run-up in the Karstadt share price, Handelsblatt said.
WCM has repeatedly denied having an interest in Karstadt, but market rumours have persisted that it is seeking to build a stake.
Ehlerding said his company was still interested in making other acquisitions, but declined to give any details.

Karstadt, which has already announced a 1996 loss of 21 marks per share, based on the German DVFA accounting standard, and cut its dividend to 10 marks from 13, holds its annual results news conference on Thursday.

Retail sector analysts said they would be looking for details from Karstadt management on how much money its struggling Hertie store chain was losing and what the group planned to do to achieve a turnaround.

They said they also wanted to hear details of the company's plans to modernise its Karstadt outlets to meet the more successful mall-type approach adopted by its main competitor, the Metro group's Kaufhof chain.
